items.title: Bruce Johnstone interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2013
items.q: I had a wonderful reference letter from Clark Terry, who I’d played with.

ctx.x: Was it easier at that time, regarding immigration and visas and all that, than it is now?

My whole immigration thing was very odd. I came in on an H2 visa, which means the arts, and I can stay for three months, then I had to go back, tag England, and then come back. So I could go back, get my passport stamped in England, and get back on the next © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -11-

flight and come back. And then I decided that I wanted to do a green card route. And so I got a social security card and it was a matter of paying taxes, and so I got a lawyer in New York, an immigration lawyer. And I don’t think this guy was particularly good, because it took me nearly three years from the time I engaged this lawyer until I actually got the call that it had been approved.
